summary: A nailed shipping crate of horizontal planks between four corner posts, with a diagonal brace and a battened lid, parameterised by size, plank count and seed.
objective: At one metre the crate reads as posts breaking a cube, then planks with gaps and a brace, then nail domes and per-plank hue.
intent_signals: add crates to a market scene
example_prompts: Stack crates behind the market stall.
I need a cargo box I can scale from a parcel to a shipping case.
not_for: Any claim about packaging standards, load ratings or pallet dimensions.
A container with a working, openable lid.

silhouette: four corner posts standing 1.8 cm proud of every face, breaking the cube
a battened lid overhanging the box by 2 cm on all four sides
a diagonal brace crossing two opposite faces at 40 degrees
medium: four planks a side with an 11 mm gap between each pair and at both ends
lid planks running across the side planks, with two battens over them
the brace laid over the planks, not flush with them
a dark inner liner behind the plank gaps, so a gap reads as depth not as sky
fine: thirty-two dome nail heads, 2.8 cm across, two at each plank end
9 mm chamfer on every plank edge and 1.1 cm on the posts
per-plank hue jitter of 5 percent across the sixteen side planks

principles: A crate is a frame with a skin, not a box: the corner posts are what carry the silhouette once the planks flatten out at distance.
Gaps are cheaper than texture and they survive every lighting change, because a gap is a shadow the geometry casts on itself.
Nails are the smallest authored feature; they only pay off if they sit on a surface that already reads, which is why they land on the posts.
implementation: Call create({ size, planks, seed, braced }); the group is centred on its footprint with y = 0 at the ground.
Stack crates through the lid socket: it sits on the batten tops, so a stack never intersects.
Sixteen side planks and thirty-two nails are two instanced fields, so a wall of crates stays cheap.
observable_checks: Run scripts/kit-proof.py and count features in close.png: at least two from each detail-ladder band must be visible.
Two seeds differ visibly in plank tone while keeping the same silhouette.
The lid socket clears the lid battens: stacking two crates leaves no intersection.

known_limits: Authored creative geometry. Nothing here measures a real packing case or its load.
The poly budget is the triangle count observed at default parameters; six planks a side costs about 2800 triangles.
braced: false removes the diagonal and with it one medium-band feature, so the ladder claim holds only at the default.

T2 is the same geometry with runtime procedural surface and vertex occlusion (see knowledge.surface-tier-defaults); it adds no polygons and ships no files, and it reads at stylized-game quality, not photoreal.
creative_affordances: Any parameter may be pushed outside its stated range; the range is the band that was proved, not a limit.
Re-colour the planks pale and the posts dark for a tea chest, or darken everything for a powder crate.

defaults.rationale: 620 mm is the size at which a crate reads as two-handed cargo next to a 1.7 m figure, and four planks is the fewest that still shows a rhythm of gaps.

T0.note: Bevelled box from the proof log bounds; the crate is nearly its own proxy.

T2.note: Every triangle is mapped: planks, posts, braces and the dark interior take wood, the nail heads take metal. Nothing is left flat. The occlusion radius is not the 0.45 m the four pilots use: on an object only 0.68 m tall a 0.45 m radius shades most of the body at once, so it is scaled to about 0.3 of the object height (0.2 m). The 0.6 m ground-dirt band is unchanged.

T3.note: No baked glTF ships for this blueprint: phase 9C baked only the two heroes (timber-cottage and watermill).

T4.note: No external asset ships with this skill.
